newsitem.title: USA: Delta approves two stock option plans.
newsitem.headline: Delta approves two stock option plans.

text.p: Delta Air Lines said on Thursday that stockholders approved two stock option plans, giving company employees a options to purchase 24.7 million shares of common stock.
The company said it also adopted a new shareholder rights plan to replace an existing one that was set to expire on November 4.
The stock option plans are intended to cover substantially all of its non-officer personnel. One is for about 47,000 Dela employees who are not pilots, while the other covers about 8,000 pilots.
The plans combined provide for the grant of non-qualified stock options to purchase 24.7 million shares of Delta common stock.
Non-pilots will be granted options for 14.7 million shares, while pilots will be granted options for 10 million shares. The stock option grants will be made in three equal annual installments.

Under the new shareholder rights plan, each stockholder will receive a dividend of one right for each share of common stock held. Each right entitles the holder to purchase from the company 1/100th of a share of a new series of preferred stock at an initial purchase price of $300.
The rights are exercisable after any individual or group acquires 15 percent or more of Delta's common stock.
